subject: Throughput sizing follow-up: tokens/sec, concurrency, streaming requirements
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finex-pay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-01T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up & post-call notes: throughput sizing

Alex — thanks for the session earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps on sizing for the FinEx pilot:

Summary of what you shared:
- Primary use: real-time payment chat assistant + transaction summarization called by backend API.
- Typical prompt length (incl. system + user): ~120 tokens. Expected response size: 80–220 tokens.
- Expected steady-state QPS: ~8 requests/sec during business hours.
- Peak bursts: up to 60 req/sec for short windows (1–3 minutes) during batch notifications.
- Hard latency SLO: 250 ms p95 for short responses; soft target 150 ms p50 for interactive flows.
- Streaming: wanted for progressive token emission for chat UI (yes).
- Auth/PII: all traffic stays within your VPC/Dedicated environment for pilot.

Initial sizing estimates (ballpark):
- Model: we recommend r-instruct-13B-quant for parity with current quality.
- Tokens/sec: measured throughput for similar workloads is ~1,200 token/s per GPU in steady-state for 128-context streaming workloads. That maps to ~10–12 concurrent requests at avg 150 tokens total.
- Concurrency / QPS mapping: to sustain 60 QPS peak with streaming, estimate ~5 dedicated GPUs with autoscale buffer. For steady-state 8 QPS, 1–2 GPUs with autoscaling headroom looks sufficient.
- Latency: with continuous batching disabled for streaming, expect 120–220 ms p50/p95 on optimized rigs; tail depends on contention/queueing.

Attachments: I attached a short PDF with the detailed throughput table and the sample workload you shared (we used your CSV to run a quick run-rate calc).

Next steps:
1) Marissa to run a quick micro-benchmark using your sample CSV to refine tokens/sec and concurrency numbers (ETA 48 hours).
2) Alex/PM to confirm which flows require strict p95 250 ms vs best-effort (helps sizing).
3) If FinEx wants a pilot SLA, we can propose Dedicated capacity with canary routing for the first 30 days.

Anything I missed? Happy to adjust numbers after Marissa's micro-bench.

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finex-pay.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@finex-pay.com>
Date: 2026-07-02T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up & post-call notes: throughput sizing

Thanks, Rafael — this is really helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

- Latency SLO: the product team is targeting 200 ms p95 for the chat UX, but the compliance team will accept up to 300 ms during initial pilot. We'll aim for 200 ms.
- Streaming: yes please — we need chunked token emission to the client for typing indicator and partial responses.
- Peak pattern: the 60 QPS peaks are typically 2–3 minutes and happen roughly once every hour during settlement spikes.
- Auth: we'll provide a test VPC/credentials for the pilot.

Can Marissa include both streaming and non-streaming numbers in the micro-bench? Also please include the expected token-cost delta when switching from non-streaming to streaming for the same response lengths.

Alex
Alex Johnson
Senior PM, Conversational Products | FinEx Payments
alex.johnson@finex-pay.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finex-pay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-03T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up & post-call notes: throughput sizing

Hey all — running the micro-bench now against the sample workload Alex shared. A few notes so the results are actionable:

- I'll provide two tables: streaming vs non-streaming. For streaming we disable cross-request continuous batching and prioritize per-connection low-latency emission; for non-streaming we can batch 50–200ms windows to increase throughput.
- For your average response (~150 tokens), internal runs show:
  * Non-streaming (aggressive batching): ~1,400 token/s per GPU; effective concurrency ~14 reqs (150 tokens per request).
  * Streaming (low-latency path): ~950 token/s per GPU; effective concurrency ~9–10 reqs.
  * Cost delta: streaming tends to increase per-token CPU/GPU overhead by ~5–12% depending on chunk size. We'll quantify in the attached CSV.
- To meet 200 ms p95 with streaming we need to cap per-GPU concurrency and proactively reserve 20% headroom during peaks. I will include a suggested Dedicated config (GPU count + autoscale thresholds).

I'll circulate results by EOD tomorrow (2026-07-04).

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Performance Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finex-pay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-07T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up & post-call notes: throughput sizing

Appreciate the fast turnaround and clarity — that helps a lot. Two quick asks after reviewing the draft:

1) Can you include an ops playbook for the 60 QPS spikes (runbook: scaling thresholds, alerts, and fallback to smaller model if tailing)?
2) Please call out expected p99 tail for streaming vs non-streaming so we can set realistic SLAs.

If you can include those in the final PDF and we get the cost delta numbers, Procurement will start the internal review.

Best — Alex
Alex Johnson
Senior PM, Conversational Products | FinEx Payments
